sources.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures
sources.locator: Theorem 1.1.2, printed pp. 24–26; Chapter 8 §§8.1–8.4, printed pp. 169–194, especially Proposition 8.1.8, Theorem 8.2.1 (pp. 179–181), and Theorem 8.3.1 (pp. 182–188).

contents.name: Theorem 1.1.2, Metric derivative
contents.support: The local metric-derivative theorem is proved for the assigned Euclidean W2 curve class; this result supplies the standard metric-space context.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.1, The continuity equation in R^d; Proposition 8.1.7 and Proposition 8.1.8
contents.support: The carrier proves the characteristic flow representation for the regularized Euclidean equation under its stated local ODE hypotheses.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.2, Theorem 8.2.1, Probabilistic representation
contents.support: The assigned theorem gives a complete local p=2 Euclidean proof from Gaussian regularization, tightness, lsc path energy, and the barycentric velocity identity.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.3, Theorem 8.3.1, Absolutely continuous curves and the continuity equation
contents.support: The local carrier proves the finite-action Euclidean converse estimate; the companion minimal-velocity construction is proved separately.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.4, Tangent bundle to P_p(X)
contents.support: The local Hilbert-space closure and Riesz argument supplies the Euclidean minimal-velocity conclusion.

read_evidence.inspection: Complete relevant arguments inspected in the full-text PDF; Theorem 1.1.2 and Chapter 8 §§8.1–8.4 were read in full for the claims listed above.

sources.title: Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians

contents.name: §5.1, Definition and triangle inequality
contents.support: The local proof establishes the metric axioms for Euclidean P2 and supplies a detailed gluing argument.

contents.name: §5.2, Topology induced by W_p
contents.support: The local theorem proves weak convergence plus uniform quadratic-tail control iff W2 convergence.

contents.name: §5.3.1, The Benamou–Brenier functional B_p
contents.support: The carrier fixes the distributional continuity-equation and finite-action conventions used by the assigned dynamic results.

contents.name: §5.3.2, AC curves admit velocity fields
contents.support: The local proof constructs the L2 velocity, proves its minimality, and identifies its norm with the metric derivative.

contents.name: §5.3.3, Regularization of the continuity equation
contents.support: The local Gaussian convolution argument proves the Euclidean smoothing and action bound with explicit hypotheses.

contents.name: §5.3.4, Velocity fields give Lipschitz behavior
contents.support: The local proof derives W2 absolute continuity from a finite-action continuity-equation solution.

read_evidence.inspection: Complete relevant arguments in §§5.1–5.3 were inspected, including the gluing, topology, velocity-field, regularization, and reverse-speed arguments.

sources.title: Lénaïc Chizat and Francis Bach, On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Over-parameterized Models using Optimal Transport
sources.locator: Appendix A.1, full-text PDF pp. 12–13; the W2 definition/completeness paragraph and Lemma A.1.

contents.name: Appendix A.1, Wasserstein metric and P2 completeness
contents.support: The statement confirms the P2/W2 conventions and completeness; the assigned proof is local and uses choice-explicit compactness and moment-tail arguments.

contents.name: Appendix A.1, quadratic-growth characterization of W2 convergence
contents.support: The assigned local topology theorem proves this characterization with explicit uniform-tail hypotheses.

contents.name: Lemma A.1, Wasserstein continuity of F
contents.support: This lemma concerns continuity of the paper-specific functional F under Assumptions 2.1; the assigned metric and continuity-equation claims do not use that functional or its hypotheses.
contents.reason: This lemma concerns continuity of the paper-specific functional F under Assumptions 2.1; the assigned metric and continuity-equation claims do not use that functional or its hypotheses.

read_evidence.inspection: The full 13-page arXiv PDF was inspected; Appendix A.1 was read in full. The proceedings version was not used because it omits this appendix.

sources.title: MIT 18.102, Chapter 4, §9 Convolution
sources.locator: Chapter 4, §9 Convolution, Lemma 58 (printed pp. 136–137) and the immediately following convolution result (Eq. 4.176).

contents.name: Lemma 58, existence of a smooth positive unit-mass bump on R
contents.support: The local item supplies the complete flat-exponential proof and extends the one-dimensional construction to R^d by finite products and Tonelli.

contents.name: Equation 4.176, convolution with a smooth compactly supported function is smooth and compactly supported
contents.support: The density proof uses this smoothing fact for the compactly supported continuous approximation.

read_evidence.inspection: Read the full proof of Lemma 58, including the derivative induction at zero, normalization, and the adjacent convolution smoothness argument.
